Supertree Grove, Gardens by the Bay

Eighteen steel “trees”, 25 to 50 metres tall, carry vertical gardens, photovoltaic cells, and cooling exhausts in Singapore’s Bay South Garden.

Source
Wikipedia: Gardens by the Bay
Creator
Grant Associates, with engineering by Atelier One and Atelier Ten
Made
Bay South Garden opened 29 June 2012 (Wikipedia)
Style
Solarpunk (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Verdant, spectacular, hopeful
Evidence
Inspected the Commons photograph Singapore Gardens by the Bay Supertree Grove 22.jpg by Zairon, 4 November 2015 (original 4566 × 3003 px, viewed at 1600 × 1053 px), in a scratch folder. It is the image on the Wikidata item. The photo shows the grove by day; the night light show was not inspected.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Wikipedia: the Supertrees are 18 tree-like structures between 25 and 50 metres tall, conceived and designed by Grant Associates with the engineering of Atelier One and Atelier Ten. They are vertical gardens planted with ferns, vines, orchids, and bromeliads. Wikipedia.

Wikipedia: they carry photovoltaic cells that power some functions such as lighting, collect rainwater for irrigation and fountains, and act as air intakes and exhausts for the cooling systems of the conservatories. The OCBC Skyway joins two of the larger Supertrees. Wikipedia.

Wikimedia Commons files the park under Category:Solarpunk as an example.

Observed

  • A large Supertree has a trunk covered in climbing plants and a flared crown of dark purple steel members, branching in short angled segments.
  • Inside the crown, a white funnel-shaped core has thin green vertical ribs. Cables tie the crown to a neighbouring tree.
  • A yellow-railed elevated walkway passes the trunk at mid-height, with visitors on it.
  • Smaller Supertrees at right have planted crowns. At left, the curved glass shell of a conservatory with white arched ribs rises behind the trees.
  • Below, a dense tropical garden in bright greens. The sky is overcast white.
  • The solar cells are not legible at this scale and angle.

Why it belongs

The grove is the built version of solarpunk’s plant-and-technology hybrid: the structure takes the form of a tree, and living plants clothe it. The arched glass conservatory beside it supplies the greenhouse motif.

Its scale, purple steel, and night light show also make it a tourist spectacle. That aligns it partly with the glossy, corporate Frutiger Eco branch, so treat it as a partial fit.

Borrow

Shape a technical structure like a plant, and let real planting cover its lower part.

Combine a branching steel lattice with a smooth arched glass shell for contrast.
